# Independent review: LOGVCURV response

VERDICT: ACCEPT_FULL_V_LOG_CURVATURE_ENTRANCE_OBSTRUCTION_ONLY.

Reviewed raw response: `PROSHKA_RESPONSE_GOAL058_LOGVCURV_2026-09-16.md`, 55333 bytes, 567 LF, 0 CR, final LF, SHA-256 `e33ee8eee31a36c6b2de2e590f8c4ce94a658ed20662f505df204d7592e364f5`; imported commit `6f4da4917734c92fba9459316494dd70ebbe77b5`.

The complex-strip continuation is sound. LV5 supplies the strictly positive Hermitian diagonal by the exact reflection cancellation. Under the conditional all-row C hypothesis, the accepted Schur construction supplies PSD for each positive root on a real interval. Finite-difference derivative blocks construct the local Hilbert map; local nonvanishing around the positive diagonal, Cauchy bounds, continuation in the same Hilbert space, and monodromy yield a global holomorphic root. A finite-order pair zero then contradicts divisibility by every n.

The full-source zero construction keeps the affine `r=4 pi^2 zeta A-6 pi B` term in the Rouche budget. LV13--LV17 correctly give a zero of full f in S, and LV18--LV22 give locally uniform normalized convergence of the actual V slice to f with the physical X=0 boundary and full tail retained. Rouche therefore produces a pair zero of V, which kills only the fractional-root/log-curvature entrance.

LV23--LV27 correctly turn non-PSD C on every real open interval into a finite real row in the prescribed interval. The factorial normalization, finite-difference coefficients, and `-2+hB<-1` budget are consistent. This is an existential finite row, with no claimed rank or numerical nodes.

Verified the four cited report bytes at SOURCE_BASE `15c6ef56f190975eb945ccec50e53a9b44d2a74b`; their SHA-256 pins match. The result does not establish a negative row of V, failure of ordinary Gram positivity, or any RH statement. The prior positive two-end limiting curvature result is compatible with this all-rank obstruction.
source_zero_review_text:
# Source-zero audit for the full-theta V response

STATUS: Sections 3, 5, and 6 pass the requested normalization audit. They give
a full-source zero of f in the strip and transfer it to a pair zero of the full
complex integral V. These are source/profile zeros, not xi zeros and not a
direct finite negative row. The final curvature obstruction still uses the
all-rank root/zero lemma in section 4 of the response.

## Source pin and scope

Audited response:

gamma-reciprocity-worktree/docs/routeB_bus/proshka/PROSHKA_RESPONSE_GOAL058_LOGVCURV_2026-09-16.md

SHA256:
e33ee8eee31a36c6b2de2e590f8c4ce94a658ed20662f505df204d7592e364f5

The audit is limited to printed sections 3, 5, and 6, locators (LV2)--(LV5)
and (LV12)--(LV22). No numerical zero search or xi-zero claim is used.

## Section 3: complex holomorphy and the positive Hermitian diagonal

On
  S = {z : |Im z| < pi/4},   f(z) = A^(-1) exp(5z/2) r(exp(2z)),
the stated compact-set estimate (LV2) is the right majorant: on a compact Q
in S, Re(exp(2z)) has a positive lower bound, so every fixed derivative of
the complete theta series has an integrable endpoint bound. It justifies
joint holomorphy of

  V(z,w) = integral_0^infinity (2X+z+w) f(X+z) f(X+w) dX

on S x S, with the linear weight retained.

For z=a+ib, the Hermitian diagonal calculation is exact:

  V(conjugate(z),z)
    = 2 integral_a^infinity u |f(u+ib)|^2 du
    = 2 integral_|a|^infinity u |f(u+ib)|^2 du > 0.          (LV5)

The second equality uses |f(-u+ib)| = |f(u+ib)| and cancellation of the odd
factor u on [a,-a] when a<0. Strictness only uses that the analytic profile
is not identically zero on a horizontal ray. This is positivity of the
complex Hermitian diagonal, not all-row positivity.

## Section 5: the 1/64, 1/31, and Rouché checks

The full source decomposition (LV12) is exact:

  r(zeta) = 4 pi^2 [ zeta A(zeta) - (3/(2 pi)) B(zeta) ],
  A(zeta) = sum_{n>=1} n^4 exp(-pi n^2 zeta),
  B(zeta) = sum_{n>=1} n^2 exp(-pi n^2 zeta),

and both A and B are 2i-periodic. The factor zeta in r is not periodic; the
later Rouché normalization correctly retains it.

At zeta=a+i, the complete alternating series satisfies
A(a+i) = Theta_4''(a)/(2 pi^2). The Jacobi expansion (LV13) gives the exact
formula (LV14), with c_j = pi(2j+1)^2/4:

  A(a+i) = a^(-9/2)/pi^2 sum_{j>=0} exp(-c_j/a)
           (c_j^2 - 3 c_j a + 3 a^2/4).                    (R3)

For a_minus = pi/16 = c_0/4, a_minus/c_j <= 1/4, and
1 - 3y + 3y^2/4 >= 1/4 on 0 <= y <= 1/4. The j=0 term therefore contributes

  a_minus^(-9/2) exp(-4) c_0^2/(4 pi^2)
  = (1/64) a_minus^(-9/2) exp(-4) > 0,                     (R4)

because c_0 = pi/4 and c_0^2/(4 pi^2) = 1/64. Thus the printed 1/64 is
correctly normalized and uses the complete Jacobi series.

At a_plus = 1, the n=1 term is -exp(-pi). For n>=2,
n^4 <= 16^(n-1) and n^2-1 >= 3(n-1), while pi>3 and e>2 imply

  q = 16 exp(-9) < 1/32,
  sum_{n>=2} n^4 exp(-pi(n^2-1)) <= q/(1-q) < 1/31.        (R5)

Factoring exp(-pi) from the tail gives

  A(1+i) < -exp(-pi) + exp(-pi)/31
         = -(30/31) exp(-pi) < 0.                          (R6)

So the printed 1/31 is valid; it is a geometric-series bound for the entire
tail, not a first-mode numerical approximation. Continuity gives a real
a_0 in (pi/16,1) with A(a_0+i)=0.

Let zeta_0=a_0+i and choose a small circle on which A has no zeros. With m_A
its positive boundary minimum and M_A the boundary maximum of
|zeta A-(3/(2pi))B|, periodicity gives exactly

  r(zeta+2ik)/(8 pi^2 i k)
    = A(zeta) + [zeta A(zeta)-(3/(2pi))B(zeta)]/(2 i k).    (R7)

For k>M_A/m_A, the perturbation is at most M_A/(2k)<m_A/2. Rouché therefore
produces a zero t_k of the full r, including B, with Re(t_k)>0 and Im(t_k)>0.
The principal half-logarithm lies in S and gives f(z_k)=0. No xi function
occurs in this construction: the zero is a zero of the theta density/profile,
and its existence neither contradicts nor proves RH.

## Section 6: exact lambda_x normalization and pair-zero transfer

For real t>=1, the full source tail factors as (LV18)

  r(t) = 4 pi^2 t exp(-pi t) H(t),
  H(t) = 1 - 3/(2 pi t) + R(t),

with 0 <= R(t) <= C_* exp(-3 pi t). Hence
H(t) >= h_minus = 1 - 3/(2 pi) > 0 and the denominator used below is positive.

The local scale is correctly

  lambda_x = 2 pi exp(2x),
  B_x(z) = lambda_x V(x,z) / (x f(x)).                       (R8)

Indeed, with v=lambda_x X, direct substitution gives the exact identity (LV19)

  B_x(z) = integral_0^infinity
    (1 + z/x + 2v/(lambda_x x))
    [f(x+v/lambda_x)/f(x)] f(z+v/lambda_x) dv.                (R9)

The factor 2X and the lower endpoint X=0 are retained. From the full tail
factorization,

  f(x+t)/f(x)
    = exp(9t/2 - pi exp(2x)(exp(2t)-1))
      H(exp(2x+2t))/H(exp(2x)).                               (R10)

Since exp(2t)-1 >= 2t, lambda_x>=9 yields the uniform majorant

  0 < f(x+v/lambda_x)/f(x)
      <= (1+C_*)/h_minus * exp(-v/2).                         (R11)

For compact Q subset S, f(z+t) is uniformly bounded for z in Q and t>=0.
Thus the integrand is dominated by C_Q(1+v) exp(-v/2), and pointwise,
uniformly on Q, the ratio tends to exp(-v) while
f(z+v/lambda_x) tends to f(z). Dominated convergence gives

  B_x(z) -> f(z) locally uniformly on S.                     (R12)

No differentiation of an asymptotic remainder is used.

Choose a disk around one zero of f from section 5, compactly contained in S,
with no boundary zero. Rouché applied to (R12) gives, for some sufficiently
large real x>0, a point w in S with

  V(x,w)=0,   V(x,x)>0.                                      (R13)

The second statement follows from the positive real diagonal and ensures that
the slice is not identically zero. This is a zero of the full complex
integral V; it is not a zero of xi and is not itself a negative real finite
row.

## Verdict and exact remaining dependency

The constants 1/64, 1/31, the 2i period, the Rouché normalization, and the
lambda_x = 2 pi exp(2x) tail scale all check. Sections 3, 5, and 6 therefore
provide a source-verified complex pair-zero mechanism for full V, with no
first-mode truncation and no RH assertion.

The implication from this pair zero to failure of C_V PSD on every real open
interval is not contained in sections 3, 5, and 6 alone: it depends on section
4's conditional all-rank lemma, namely that PSD of every positive root on an
open real interval extends along the positive Hermitian diagonal and forbids
any pair zero in S x S. Subject to that separately audited lemma, (R13) is a
complete obstruction to the all-row logarithmic-curvature route. It does not
establish a direct negative row for V, nor anything about xi-zero locations or
RH.
